newsitem.title: USA: Calif. land developer held over for trial - official.
newsitem.headline: Calif. land developer held over for trial - official.

text.p: A magistrate in San Mateo County, Calif., ruled Thursday that there was probable cause to hold a former developer linked to two failed land deals over for trial, the district attorney's office said.
"I'm very pleased," Chuck Finney, deputy district attorney for San Mateo County, said of the decision, which came at the end of a lengthy preliminary hearing.

The magistrate said the former developer, G. Michael Montross, should be held over for trial in Superior Court, and scheduled his arraignment for December 27, Finney said. At that hearing, a trial date was expected to be set.
Montross is being held in the San Mateo County jail.

More than two years ago, the San Mateo County District Attorney filed 93 counts of state securities violations against Montross related to two failed land developments, including one in Nevada County, Calif., that involved bonds.

After more than two years on the run, Montross was taken into custody in June. He has pleaded not guilty to all of the San Mateo County charges. His attorney was not immediately available to comment after Thursday's court session.
Currently, there are 87 counts against Montross, Finney said. The other counts were dropped.

The Montross case has attracted the attention of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission even though the charges brought by the district attorney do not specifically involve the Nevada County bonds.

The Nevada County bonds are the subject of a broad SEC investigation, which has focused on the county, underwriter First California Capital Markets Group Inc and other bond professionals involved in the deal.

Montross was recently subpoenaed by the SEC to answer questions about the Nevada County bonds. Montross met with the SEC, but refused to answer questions about the bonds, David Packard, an attorney for Montross, said in a November interview.
